title: Real Madrid have a plan to stop Barcelona: Spending more money than they did in 2010
summary: Real Madrid, led by president Florentino Perez and manager Jose Mourinho, plan a major summer spending spree to challenge Barcelona's recent dominance. Having already signed several players, reports suggest Madrid are targeting Yan Diomande and Rodri in deals that could surpass their 2010 rebuild. Barcelona are operating more cautiously and relying on La Masia and a smaller set of signings. The looming transfer battle sets the stage for a renewed rivalry in LaLiga.
content:
Barcelona have enjoyed a period of dominance over Spanish football in the last two seasons, winning five of the six domestic titles on offer, including back-to-back La Liga crowns.

That success has clearly stung Real Madrid, and president Florentino Perez is now preparing to spend big in an effort to shift the balance of power back in their favour. According to Mundo Deportivo, the scale of Real Madrid's spending this summer could even surpass the famous 2010 rebuild, when Perez last turned to Jose Mourinho to dethrone a great Barcelona side.

Real Madrid have already been active this window, signing Ibrahima Konate and Bernardo Silva on free transfers, and paying €60 million for Marc Cucurella and €20 million for Denzel Dumfries. Reports suggest the club are ready to spend more than €100 million on RB Leipzig winger Yan Diomande, while a further nine-figure move for Manchester City's Rodri is also being lined up.

Should both deals go through, this summer's outlay would comfortably eclipse the €182.2 million Real Madrid spent last year on the likes of Franco Mastantuono, Dean Huijsen, Alvaro Carreras and Trent Alexander-Arnold, none of whom have yet secured a regular role.

The parallels with 2010 are hard to ignore. Back then, Perez appointed Mourinho and surrounded him with Angel Di Maria, Mesut Ozil, Sami Khedira and Ricardo Carvalho in an attempt to topple Pep Guardiola's Barcelona. Perez has once again hired the same coach, reportedly paying €15 million to release Mourinho from Benfica, and is offering the Portuguese even greater backing than he had 16 years ago.

Barcelona, by contrast, continue to operate within their financial limitations and lean heavily on La Masia. Their business this summer has been comparatively restrained, with Anthony Gordon arriving from Newcastle for €70 million and Karim Adeyemi joining from Borussia Dortmund for €22 million. With the Julian Alvarez saga still unresolved, the stage is set for a familiar showdown: Mourinho's expensively assembled Real Madrid against a Barcelona side determined to protect the dominance they have fought so hard to establish.

If the reported targets and sums materialise, this transfer window could reshape the balance of power in LaLiga and set up another high-stakes chapter in the historic Madrid-Barcelona rivalry. Both clubs face different constraints and strategies: Real with heavy investment and a clear deadline to challenge immediately, Barcelona with sustainable spending and an emphasis on youth development. The coming weeks will reveal whether Real's gamble pays off and how Barcelona respond on and off the pitch.
